```{r setup}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Category (National) Scorecard — branded, paginated "Download" report
#
# Rendered on demand by the Shiny app's download_cat handler in ADA_PARC.Rmd,
# with the same params (category, year, palette, contrast) the reader
# selected on screen. This document does NOT recompute scores: it calls
# build_category_scorecard() in category_scorecard_core.R, the same function
# category_scorecard.qmd (the on-screen version) calls, so the two can never
# report different numbers for the same category. See the header comment in
# category_scorecard_core.R.
#
# The one presentation choice this document makes on its own: the on-screen
# choropleth is an interactive ggiraph widget (hover tooltips per state);
# this document exports the SAME underlying ggplot object (p_map) to a
# static SVG via svglite instead, the technique the National Data map
# download already uses. Everything else unique to this document -- the
# ADA-PARC brand masthead, grant funding footer, and print/pagination CSS --
# follows the same pattern as state_scorecard_print.qmd.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
options(cli.width = 80)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dpi = 96, fig.retina = 2)

library(htmltools)
library(ggplot2)

local({
  cand <- c("category_scorecard_core.R",
            file.path("scorecard", "category_scorecard_core.R"))
  hit  <- cand[file.exists(cand)]
  if (length(hit) == 0) {
    stop("category_scorecard_print.qmd cannot locate category_scorecard_core.R. ",
         "Render with execute_dir set to the scorecard/ directory, ",
         "or from the project root.")
  }
  source(hit[1], local = FALSE)
})

ctx <- build_category_scorecard(
  category = params$category,
  year     = params$year,
  palette  = params$palette,
  contrast = params$contrast
)
# invisible() matters here: list2env() returns the environment it just
# populated (this chunk's own environment == R_GlobalEnv when this document
# is rendered from the Shiny app's download handler), and as the last
# expression in the chunk it would otherwise auto-print. That auto-print is
# exactly the stray "<environment: R_GlobalEnv>" line that used to appear
# above the masthead on every rendered scorecard. Same fix already applied
# in state_scorecard.qmd / state_scorecard_print.qmd; this file and
# category_scorecard.qmd had fallen out of sync with that fix until now.
invisible(list2env(ctx, environment()))
```

```{css}
   Fixed ADA-PARC brand maroon/gold, not the reader's chosen palette: the

}

/* ── Static map figure ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.map-figure { margin: 0.5rem 0 0.5rem 0; text-align: center; }
.map-figure svg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }

/* ── Pagination ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
@page {
  size: Letter;
  margin: 0.6in 0.5in;
}
.print-page-break {
  break-before: page;
  page-break-before: always;
}

@media print {
  /* Same Chromium CSS-grid fragmentation fix as the National/City/State
     downloads. See feedback_quarto_print_pagination memory. */
  #quarto-content,
  #quarto-content.page-columns,
  .page-columns,
  main.content,
  main#quarto-document-content,
  .cell {
    display: block !important;
    grid-template-columns: none !important;
  }

  .print-bar { display: none !important; }
  #gt-table-note-search { display: none !important; }

  body { font-size: 11pt; }

  body,
  .adaparc-banner {
    -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
    print-color-adjust: exact;
  }

  .adaparc-banner { padding: 0.6rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.7rem; }
  .adaparc-banner .banner-icon { height: 26px; }

  .adaparc-footer {
    break-inside: avoid;
    /* Was 8pt. Bumped to keep the funding note above ~9.5pt printed, in
       line with the project's accessibility minimum-font-size bar -- 8pt
       reads uncomfortably small on paper even for a footer, which sits
       oddly on a disability-rights research center's own deliverable.
       Same fix already applied in state_scorecard_print.qmd. */
    font-size: 9.5pt;
    margin-top: 0.6rem;
    padding-top: 0.4rem;
  }
  .adaparc-footer p { margin: 0.1rem 0; }

  /* Each card is the unit a reader reasons about. */
  .section-card, .stat-pills {
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
  }

  /* ...but NOT the rankings cards. Those are deliberately one-page-each by
     construction (see the row-budget chunk below), and asking an engine to
     keep a card intact that is already sized to fill its page is asking for
     the artifact Colin's 2026-08-20 PDF showed: Safari honoured the rule as
     far as it could, then fragmented anyway and stranded the card's own
     rounded bottom edge alone at the top of the FOLLOWING page (twice, on
     printed pages 4 and 6). Releasing the constraint here removes the
     contradiction. */
  .section-card.rankings-section {
    break-inside: auto !important;
    page-break-inside: auto !important;
  }

  /* The rankings table opens its own page rather than starting a few lines
     from the bottom of the map section. Reused (same class) on the
     continuation block below, so it also opens on its own page. */
  .rankings-section { break-before: page; page-break-before: always; }

  /* Print-only card treatment for the rankings pages, doing two jobs.
     (1) No border/radius/shadow, so there is no rounded box edge that CAN
     be stranded on a following page even if something does fragment; the
     table's own accent top border and dark header row carry the structure
     on paper perfectly well.
     (2) No left/right padding, which hands the table the full ~7.5in
     printable width instead of ~7.0in. That extra ~0.5in is what lets the
     widest sub-index label ("Living Arrangements") sit on its own line
     rather than being wrapped and then clipped -- see the column-width
     rules further down. Reduced top padding buys back ~1 row of budget. */
  .section-card.rankings-section {
    border: 0 !important;
    border-radius: 0 !important;
    box-shadow: none !important;
    padding: 0.6rem 0 0.6rem !important;
    margin-bottom: 0 !important;
  }

  /* A rankings heading must never be the last thing on a page with its
     table starting on the next one. Same lesson as the city profile
     download's stranded h3 subheads. */
  .rankings-section h2,
  .rankings-section .section-sub {
    break-after: avoid !important;
    page-break-after: avoid !important;
  }

  /* "(continued)" label on the second/later table-page heading. Matches the
     grey the same pattern uses in national_topic.qmd. */
  .continued { font-weight: 500; color: #666; }

  /* 2026-08-19: the rankings table used to be ONE 51-row gt table, relying
     on Chromium/WebKit to fragment the <table> across pages and repeat its
     <thead> via the display:table-header-group rules just below. A
     rendered PDF showed that failing outright past the first page --
     WebKit does not reliably repeat an auto-fragmented thead, the same gap
     national_topic.qmd's own comments already document for the National
     Data download. Fixed the same way that file fixes it: split the ranked
     rows into 2 REAL, separate gt tables (each with its own <thead>, built
     by build_rankings_gt() in category_scorecard_core.R and printed as two
     static page blocks below -- see the long comment there for why not a
     loop), instead of one long table plus CSS hoping the browser repeats
     it. At the current 9.5pt / tightened-padding row height this yields
     2 pages for a 51-row category, matching every category today; the
     assertions in the rankings-table-build chunk fail the render loudly
     if a page's share of rows ever exceeds what that page can physically
     hold, rather than silently spilling them onto a bare page.
     These display:table-header-group rules stay as a defensive fallback:
     if either page's own table is ever taller than expected and still
     needs to fragment across a page boundary on its own, Chromium-family
     engines will still attempt to repeat that table's own thead. */
  .gt_table thead { display: table-header-group !important; }
  .gt_table tbody { display: table-row-group !important; }
  .gt_table tfoot { display: table-footer-group !important; }

  /* Tightened, print-only row/header padding (on-screen keeps gt's default
     5px data_row.padding). Shrinks the vertical footprint of each row.
     3px was measured at a 20.8pt row pitch in Colin's 2026-08-20 export;
     2px takes that to roughly 19.3pt, which is where the row budgets in
     the rankings-table-build chunk below come from. Font size is NOT
     touched (stays 9.5pt) so this costs nothing in readability. */
  .gt_table .gt_row { padding-top: 2px !important; padding-bottom: 2px !important; }
  .gt_table .gt_col_heading { padding-top: 5px !important; padding-bottom: 5px !important; }

  /* break-inside: avoid on <tr> is not reliably honoured by every Chromium
     build once a cell's text wraps to two lines (confirmed 2026-08-19: a
     downloaded PDF split "North Carolina" as "North" on one page and
     "Carolina" on the next, mid-row). Declared !important, with both the
     legacy and Level-4 fragmentation property, and repeated on the cells
     themselves as well as the row, since some engines respect it on one but
     not the other. This narrows the failure window; it is a mitigation for
     a browser limitation the site's CSS cannot fully guarantee against
     (see the print-hint copy below), not a 100% fix. The column-width fix
     just below also reduces how often a state name needs to wrap onto a
     second line in the first place, which is the other lever available
     here. */
  .gt_table tr {
    break-inside: avoid !important;
    break-inside: avoid-page !important;
    page-break-inside: avoid !important;
  }
  .gt_table td, .gt_table th {
    break-inside: avoid !important;
    page-break-inside: avoid !important;
  }
  .gt_table { font-size: 9.5pt; }

  /* gt's cols_width() (category_scorecard_core.R) sets fixed pixel widths
     tuned for the on-screen table, where a wide category (e.g. Community
     Participation's 5 sub-indices) is allowed to horizontal-scroll. Print
     has no scrollbar: with the default auto table layout, a browser treats
     those px widths as minimums and expands the table past the page's
     ~7.5in printable width instead of shrinking to fit, silently pushing
     the rightmost column(s) (Housing Access, sometimes Community Resource
     too) off the printed page entirely. Confirmed by rendering the real gt
     table through Chromium print-to-PDF: Housing Access was fully absent
     and Community Resource was cut mid-column with this rule missing.
     table-layout: fixed makes the browser treat the specified widths as
     proportional hints and scale every column down to fit table.width
     (100%, already set by tab_options()) instead, so all columns stay
     visible. Print-scoped only (this document's own CSS block, not
     scorecard_v3.css) so the on-screen table's sizing is unaffected. */
  .gt_table { table-layout: fixed !important; width: 100% !important; }

  /* Setting every <col> to width:auto (an earlier version of this rule)
     backfired: per the CSS2.1 fixed-table-layout algorithm, when ALL
     columns are auto and no first-row cell carries an explicit width, the
     browser divides the table equally among every column, so
     State/Territory (originally the widest column, 155px, sized to fit
     "Massachusetts"/"District of Columbia") shrank to the same width as
     Abbrev. (48px) and "Massachusetts" was clipped to "Massachuset".
     Fix: give the leading text columns explicit percentages (by column
     POSITION, since gt does not add a class per column) and leave the
     numeric columns auto, so they divide the remainder evenly among
     themselves whether the category has 3 sub-indices or 5.

     2026-08-20, renumbered: the print table no longer has an Abbrev.
     column (build_rankings_gt(drop_abbrev = TRUE) in the build chunk
     below), so every numeric column moved one position left and these
     selectors had to move with it. The 7% Abbrev. share was redistributed
     to State/Territory and to the numeric columns, which is what buys the
     sub-index headers enough room. If you ever put Abbrev. back, these
     four selectors have to shift right again. */
  .gt_table col:nth-child(1) { width: 8%  !important; }  /* Rank */
  .gt_table col:nth-child(2) { width: 12% !important; }  /* Tier */
  .gt_table col:nth-child(3) { width: 24% !important; }  /* State / Territory */
  .gt_table col:nth-child(n+4) { width: auto !important; } /* CL Score + sub-indices */

  /* THE actual cause of the clipped column headers in Colin's 2026-08-20
     export ("Abbrev" cut mid-word, "Living Arrangement" cut on its second
     line). It was never the widths on their own: gt ships
     `overflow-x: hidden` on .gt_col_heading as well as on .gt_row, and the
     override below only ever covered .gt_row -- so body cells were safe
     and the header cells silently lost characters. Fixing the widths alone
     would have papered over this until the next category with a longer
     sub-index label. white-space: normal is explicit because a header that
     needs two lines must be allowed to take two lines rather than being
     held on one and cut. */
  .gt_table .gt_row,
  .gt_table .gt_col_heading {
    overflow: visible !important;
    overflow-wrap: anywhere;
    white-space: normal !important;
  }

  /* The gt table's <caption> (tab_caption() in category_scorecard_core.R)
     duplicates the "State Rankings" heading and intro sentence already
     printed above the table, just reworded, immediately after row 51. It
     is a genuine semantic <caption> that screen readers use to describe
     the table, so it stays in the document rather than being deleted --
     only visually hidden here, print-scoped, with the standard
     clip-rect technique (not display:none, which some assistive tech also
     hides) so sighted print readers stop seeing the repeated text but nothing
     is removed from the accessibility tree. */
  .gt_table caption {
    position: absolute;
    width: 1px;
    height: 1px;
    padding: 0;
    margin: -1px;
    overflow: hidden;
    clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
    white-space: nowrap;
    border: 0;
  }

  /* The methodology note and the NIDILRR funding acknowledgment are one
     closing block, and in the 2026-08-20 export the funding block alone
     was pushed onto a ninth page with nothing else on it. Grouping them
     under one break-inside: avoid keeps them together at the foot of the
     About This Category page. */
  .footer-note {
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
    break-after: avoid;
    page-break-after: avoid;
  }

  a[href]:after { content: ""; }
}
```

```{r banner, results='asis'}
  'Print or save as PDF</button>',
  # Chrome/Edge/Firefox print dialogs default "Headers and footers" ON,
  # which stamps the browser tab title, local file path, timestamp, and a
  # generic page count across every page of an otherwise branded document
  # -- exactly what showed up on every page of the uploaded PDF this fix
  # was made from. CSS cannot suppress that (it is dialog UI, not page
  # content), so this is a nudge to turn it off rather than a silent gap.
  # Re-styled 2026-08-19 as a bordered callout with the key action bolded
  # (was a single line of small grey text easy to skim past -- the exact
  # PDF this fix responds to was generated with the setting left on). Same
  # fix already applied in state_scorecard_print.qmd.
  '<p class="print-hint"><strong>Before saving: turn &ldquo;Headers and ',
  'footers&rdquo; OFF</strong> in the print dialog&rsquo;s More settings. ',
  'Otherwise your browser stamps a local file path and timestamp across ',
  'every page of this report.</p>',
  '</div>\n'
))
```

<!-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     MAP (static SVG, not the interactive ggiraph widget)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->
::: {.section-card}

<h2 style="`r heading_style`">State Scores — `r cfg$name`</h2>
<p class="section-sub">States divided into four equal-population quartile groups. Alaska, Hawaii, D.C., and territories appear in the rankings table below.</p>

```{r map-svg, results='asis'}
# Same p_map ggplot object the on-screen scorecard wraps in girafe() for
# hover tooltips (category_scorecard_core.R). Exported here to static SVG via
# svglite instead -- the same technique ADA_PARC.Rmd's National Data map
# download already uses for render_national_map(). svglite emits the
# requested font-family; the browser pairs it with the EB Garamond webfont
# loaded via font-loader.html.
svg_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = svg_tmp, plot = p_map,
  device = svglite::svglite,
  width = 10, height = 6.2, bg = "white"
)
svg_lines <- readLines(svg_tmp, warn = FALSE)
# Drop svglite's leading XML declaration (`<?xml version='1.0' ...?>`)
# before handing this off to cat(). Browsers don't need it for inline SVG,
# and leaving it in front of a raw `results='asis'` HTML block breaks
# Pandoc's block parser badly enough that it loses track of the enclosing
# `::: {.section-card}` fence: both the opening and closing ::: markers
# for this card printed as literal, visible text ("::: {.section-card}")
# on the rendered page instead of becoming a real <div>, while everything
# else (including the map itself) still rendered correctly. Isolated with
# a minimal pandoc repro -- this one line was the exact trigger, and
# increasing the fence's colon count did NOT fix it, only removing this
# line did.
svg_lines <- svg_lines[!grepl("^<\\?xml", svg_lines)]
map_svg <- paste(svg_lines, collapse = "\n")
unlink(svg_tmp)

map_alt <- paste0(
  "Choropleth map of the United States showing ", cfg$name,
  " scores by state, divided into four quartile tiers from Poor to ",
  "Excellent. Highest score: ", top_row$NAME, " at ", f(top_row$cat_overall),
  ". Lowest score: ", bot_row$NAME, " at ", f(bot_row$cat_overall), "."
)

cat('<div class="map-figure" role="img" aria-label="',
    htmltools::htmlEscape(map_alt, attribute = TRUE), '">\n', sep = "")
cat(map_svg)
cat('\n</div>\n')
```

<p class="map-caption">Scores range 0–100; higher is better. Grey indicates states with no data in this render.</p>

:::

<!-- ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     RANKINGS TABLE
     print-page-break + .rankings-section: opens on its own page. No live
     search box in the downloaded report -- it has no purpose in a static
     file and the print CSS above hides it defensively either way.

     Split across 2 real gt tables (one per printed page, each with its own
     header row) rather than one continuous table -- see the long comment
     on .gt_table thead in the {css} block above for why.

     2026-08-19, second pass: the first version of this fix manually
     cat()'d gt::as_raw_html() output inside a results='asis' chunk nested
     in a ::: fenced Div. Colin's next render showed literal "::: {...}"
     and stray ":::" text leaking onto pages 1, 2, 3 and 7 -- Pandoc's
     fenced-Div tracking got desynced for the REST of the document, not
     just around the table. Diagnosis: gt's pretty-printed HTML contains
     blank lines (inside its own <style> block, between table sections),
     and a blank line inside a raw HTML block being cat()'d into a
     results='asis' chunk ends Pandoc's raw-HTML-block scan early
     (CommonMark HTML block type 6 terminates at the first blank line
     it sees) -- everything after that point in the string gets fed back
     through the Markdown block parser instead of passed through verbatim,
     which is what threw off the ::: fence-nesting count for everything
     downstream. Same bug FAMILY as the svglite XML-declaration fence-leak
     already fixed in the map-svg chunk below (see
     [[project_category_scorecard_print_bugfixes]]), different trigger.
     Fix: stop hand-building raw HTML strings for the tables entirely.
     Each page's gt table is instead simply the last value of its own
     ordinary (non-results='asis') chunk -- exactly how the single
     51-row `gt_table` rendered before this whole print-pagination change,
     which never leaked. knitr/gt's own print method (not a raw HTML
     string this file constructs and cat()s) handles it safely.
     Consequence: the two pages are written out as two static blocks below
     rather than generated in a loop, since a dynamically-sized run of
     markdown+chunk blocks isn't something a single knitr execution can
     emit. All three categories have 51 populated rows today, always
     exactly 2 pages; the assertions in the setup chunk below fail the
     render loudly (instead of silently dropping or spilling a page of
     states) if that ever stops being true.

     2026-08-20, third pass. Colin's export still broke, and the cause was
     the row budget itself, not the table-splitting mechanism. The old
     ROWS_PER_PAGE = 27 was copied from national_topic.qmd, whose table
     pages carry different chrome, and it was never measured against THIS
     document. Measured from the actual export (Letter 612x792pt, @page
     margin 0.6in, so usable y runs 43.2 to 748.8):

       printed page 1  first data row top y = 256.7  ->  23 rows fit
       printed page 2  first data row top y = 191.9  ->  25 rows + note fit

     The code was feeding page 1 twenty-six rows. Rows 24 to 26 spilled
     onto a bare page with no header row and no card, and one row was
     painted as a fragment at the page foot. Worse, the two pages never had
     equal capacity: page 1 alone carried the gt tab_header title bar plus
     a two-line intro, 64.8pt of extra chrome, about three rows' worth. A
     single symmetric constant could not have been right for both.
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ -->

```{r rankings-table-build}
# ── Measured row budgets ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Derived, not inherited. Do not copy these numbers into another document;
# re-measure there. Arithmetic, all in points:
#
#   usable page height        792 - (2 x 43.2)          = 705.6   (y 43.2..748.8)
#   chrome above first row    card pad + h2 + 1-line sub + 2-line
#                             column header               ~ 132
#     (measured 148.7 in the 2026-08-20 export, minus ~17 saved by the
#      reduced print card padding in the {css} block above)
#   row pitch                 9.5pt text + 2px padding    ~ 19.3
#     (measured 20.8 at the old 3px padding)
#   source note block         last page only              ~ 24
#
#   page 1 capacity  (748.8 - 43.2 - 132) / 19.3          = 29.7  -> 29
#   later pages      (748.8 - 43.2 - 132 - 24) / 19.3     = 28.5  -> 28
#
# The constants below are set BELOW those figures on purpose. Safari and
# Chrome disagree slightly on text metrics, and Colin exports from Safari
# while every earlier fix in this file was validated in Chromium. Holding
# two to three rows of slack is what makes both engines land on the same
# pagination instead of one of them spilling a row. Even in the pessimistic
# case where the padding reduction does not take and the pitch stays at the
# measured 20.8, capacity is 27 and 26, so these still hold.
FIRST_PAGE_ROWS <- 27L
CONT_PAGE_ROWS  <- 26L

n_rows <- nrow(tbl_data)

# Fewest pages whose combined capacity holds every row.
n_pages <- 1L
while (FIRST_PAGE_ROWS + (n_pages - 1L) * CONT_PAGE_ROWS < n_rows) {
  n_pages <- n_pages + 1L
}

# Balance the rows evenly across those pages rather than filling page 1 to
# its cap and leaving a short last page: an even split keeps the most slack
# on every page, which is what absorbs an engine-to-engine metrics
# difference. 51 rows over 2 pages gives 26 and 25.
per_page    <- as.integer(ceiling(n_rows / n_pages))
rank_groups <- split(seq_len(n_rows), ceiling(seq_len(n_rows) / per_page))

# ── Real capacity assertions ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The previous guard was stopifnot(length(gt_pages) == 2), which only ever
# confirmed that two tables existed. It passed on the export that was
# visibly broken, because a table overflowing its page is still a table.
# These check the thing that actually matters.
page_counts <- vapply(rank_groups, length, integer(1))
budgets     <- c(FIRST_PAGE_ROWS, rep(CONT_PAGE_ROWS, length(page_counts) - 1L))

if (any(page_counts > budgets)) {
  over <- which(page_counts > budgets)
  stop(
    "category_scorecard_print.qmd: rankings table page(s) ",
    paste(over, collapse = ", "), " are over budget (",
    paste0(page_counts[over], " rows vs ", budgets[over], " allowed",
           collapse = "; "),
    "). These rows would spill onto a page with no header row. Either ",
    "re-measure the budget constants against a fresh export or reduce the ",
    "chrome above the table.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
if (sum(page_counts) != n_rows) {
  stop("category_scorecard_print.qmd: rankings pages account for ",
       sum(page_counts), " of ", n_rows, " rows.", call. = FALSE)
}

# show_title_bar = FALSE on every page now, not just continuations. The gt
# tab_header repeated the <h2>State Rankings</h2> and the intro sentence
# directly above it almost word for word, so on paper it was a third copy
# of the same text -- and it cost ~46pt, over two rows of budget, on the
# one page that could least afford it. tab_caption() still carries the
# table's description for screen readers (visually hidden in print, see
# the {css} block above), so nothing is lost from the accessibility tree.
#
# drop_abbrev = TRUE: print only. The state name is spelled out in the
# adjacent column, and the ~7% of width the two-letter code was taking is
# what the sub-index headers needed to stop being clipped. See the long
# comment on build_rankings_gt() in category_scorecard_core.R.
gt_pages <- lapply(seq_along(rank_groups), function(k) {
  idx <- rank_groups[[k]]
  build_rankings_gt(
    tbl_data[idx, , drop = FALSE],
    tier_rows_for(idx),
    show_title_bar   = FALSE,
    show_source_note = (k == length(rank_groups)),
    drop_abbrev      = TRUE
  )
})

# The two page blocks below are static markdown, not generated in a loop
# (see the long comment above this chunk for why a loop is not available
# here). This is the guard for THAT constraint specifically, and it is the
# reason the capacity checks above exist separately: this one is about the
# document's structure, those are about whether the rows fit.
if (length(gt_pages) != 2L) {
  stop("category_scorecard_print.qmd has exactly 2 static rankings page ",
       "blocks, but the row budget produced ", length(gt_pages),
       " page(s) for ", n_rows, " rows. Add or remove a page block below ",
       "to match.", call. = FALSE)
}
```

     single line at print width. The second sentence that used to be here
     ("Sub-index scores are shown alongside the overall score") only
     restated what the column headers directly below already say, and it
     wrapped to a second line, costing a row of the table's page budget on
     the one page with the least to spare. -->

```{r funding-footer, results='asis'}
))
```
